ratings.reviewer_notes: Direct endothelial-cell study of evolocumab and alirocumab showing reduced IL-6, E-selectin, ICAM-1, NF-κB signaling, and monocyte adhesion, with effects involving eNOS.
Large randomized FOURIER analysis directly reports that evolocumab did not alter hsCRP at 48 weeks, although baseline hsCRP identified residual inflammatory risk.
Randomized AMI substudy directly assessed endothelial function by FMD; adding alirocumab to high-intensity statin produced no additional FMD improvement at 52 weeks.
Direct in vitro and mouse sepsis experiments found PCSK9 inhibition reduced inflammatory pathway activity and preserved eNOS, VE-cadherin, and endothelium-dependent vasodilation.
Trial assessed LDL-C lowering, feasibility, and safety during ACS but did not report inflammatory markers or endothelial-function outcomes.
Randomized controlled study directly assessed endothelial function. Evolocumab improved vasoactive range at 8 weeks, while FMD and low-flow-mediated constriction did not change.
The title concerns pleiotropic effects generally, and no abstract is available to establish evidence specifically about inflammation or endothelial function.
Direct pilot intervention study in hospitalized ACS patients found that a single evolocumab dose altered systemic inflammation, decreasing both pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines within 72 hours.

Review-level context focused on acute ischemic stroke and neuroinflammation; it describes inflammatory pathways and reports reductions in systemic hsCRP and IL-6, with limited direct evidence concerning vascular endothelial function.
